subject: Archaeology
title: Forensic Archaeology: Bones Tell Stories
description: A quick win: understand Forensic Archaeology: Bones Tell Stories.

hook.text: An archaeologist can look at a skeleton and tell you the person's age, sex, diet, diseases, and sometimes how they died.

buildup.text: Wear on joints reveals years of heavy labor. Dental cavities appeared when farming introduced sugar-rich grains.

discovery.text: Harris lines in leg bones show periods of childhood starvation.

twist.text: Forensic archaeological methods used for ancient bones are the same ones used to identify victims of modern crimes and wars.

climax.text: Archaeologists helped identify victims of the Srebrenica massacre and Argentina's Dirty War using excavation techniques.

punchline.text: The same skills that study ancient bones now bring justice to modern victims.

quiz.question: What are Harris lines in leg bones?
options: Evidence of healed fractures from childhood injuries
Scars from periods of childhood starvation where growth stopped and restarted
Lines that indicate the amount of calcium in a person's diet

details.summary: Forensic archaeology applies archaeological excavation and analysis techniques to crime scenes, mass graves, and disaster sites. Skills in skeletal analysis, stratigraphy, and evidence recovery help identify victims, determine cause of death, and reconstruct events for criminal investigations.
details.whyItMatters: Archaeological skills have direct applications in criminal justice and human rights investigations. Forensic archaeologists have helped identify genocide victims in Bosnia, Argentina, and Rwanda, bringing evidence to international tribunals.
takeaways: Applies archaeological methods to crime and disaster scenes
Skeletal analysis determines age, sex, health, and cause of death
Used in genocide investigations and international criminal tribunals

faq.question: How does forensic archaeology differ from forensic anthropology?
faq.answer: Forensic archaeology focuses on the recovery process — excavating buried remains using archaeological methods to preserve context and evidence. Forensic anthropology focuses on analyzing the remains themselves — determining identity, age, sex, and cause of death from skeletal evidence.

faq.question: How has forensic archaeology aided human rights investigations?
faq.answer: Teams have excavated mass graves in Bosnia, Guatemala, Argentina, Iraq, and Rwanda. Archaeological methods preserve evidence for war crimes tribunals by documenting body positions, blindfolds, bindings, and bullet damage in their original context, which is critical for legal prosecution.
